title: optimize-quant-kernels-int8-fp8-smoothquant-dequant-fusion-kvcache-scheduling-batching
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Quantized inference (INT8/FP8) is critical for lowering unit cost on Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments. Customers reported suboptimal throughput and latency regressions for common chat traffic shape when using smoothquant + dequant fusion paths together with KV-cache heavy workloads. This PR implements a set of coordinated runtime improvements: 1) optimized fused kernels for SmoothQuant pre/post transforms that push dequantization into the attention matmul path to avoid extra memory copies; 2) INT8/FP8 GEMM microkernel selection and a new fast path for FP8->INT8 fallback when hardware FP8 is unavailable; 3) KV-cache friendly scheduling changes that prefer co-located KV shards and reduce memory traffic during prefix-heavy workloads; 4) continuous-batching policy tweaks that reduce tail latency by dynamically shrinking batch windows for short-lived chat requests. Changeset summary: new fused kernels in runtime/ops/quant/, kernel dispatch heuristics in runtime/compile/, KV scheduler updates in runtime/scheduler/, and tests/benchmarks for A100/H100 CI. Benchmarks: microbench on H100 (context 512, batch 8) shows INT8 throughput +22% and median tail latency -18% vs prior; FP8 pathway shows +15% throughput and -12% median latency; end-to-end chat scenario with hot KV cache shows 25% higher tokens/sec and 30% lower GPU memory pressure with fusion enabled. Compatibility: preserves model semantics; added runtime flags to control fusion and fallback to previous behavior. Rollout plan: default enabled for Dedicated and Private, opt-in on hosted for first week to monitor regressions. Checklist: Tests added for correctness and numerics, CI perf jobs updated, release notes entry drafted, telemetry hooks added to track fallback rates. See linked linear tickets for rollout gating and monitoring playbook.
